author: anton_pelc
subject: Bike stolen off the platform rack
body: My gray commuter bike was taken from the rack at the Greaves Mill rail platform sometime after the 7:10 train. The U-lock was still locked to the rack, so the thief cut the rack post itself, which is new to me. The serial number is stamped under the frame and I have a photo of it. If you see a bike like this for sale, please message me. I am pretty angry about this.

comments.author: walt_gerrity
comments.body: That rack went in around 1994 and was never bolted deep enough. Your serial photo is the best thing you did all morning, son. Take it to the police non-emergency desk.

comments.author: jonah_fitch
comments.body: Sorry, Anton. It sounds like the bike thieves here are very organized, which is not a comforting thought at all.

comments.author: kofi_mensah
comments.body: Check the marketplace group and the listings near the highway on weekends. Report the serial number to the non-emergency line and ask them to flag it if it's recovered. The park board may also fix that rack if you ask.

comments.author: theo_marchetti
comments.body: Sorry, I'm new to town. Is there a used bike swap where people sell legitimate bikes? I'd like to buy one without worrying.

comments.author: casey_ostrander
comments.body: Theo, I bought mine at a swap meet in the Millrace lot last spring. The gardeners group posts bike sales too, so check there first.

comments.author: anton_pelc
comments.body: Thanks Kofi, I'll file the serial today. Ordering a bolt-in anchor kit for the rack too.

author: owen_pruitt
subject: Found orange tabby by the bus stop on Oriel Street
body: Found an orange tabby on the sidewalk by the Oriel Street bus stop this morning. He is friendly, has no collar, and looks a little thin, so he is probably someone's and not feral. He is in our garage now with water and a bowl of tuna. We can't keep him long, so if he's yours, describe him and I'll bring him over. Otherwise the vet can check him for a chip.

comments.author: june_akers
comments.body: Owen, Mulberry Fork Veterinary Clinic on Brindle Road will scan him for a chip if you bring him in, and they can look up the chip registry for the owner's number. Post a photo on the school newsletter's lost-pet page too.

comments.author: mateo_gallegos
comments.body: Lovely that you took him in. I can drive him to the clinic on my lunch break if you can't get away.

comments.author: vivian_oduya
comments.body: Forgive me, I'm new. Is there a way to tell if a cat is chipped without taking him in? Do I need to bring him?

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: He's sitting in the garage with the radio on, very relaxed. Nobody has come forward yet. Thanks, June.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: Owen, that cat has better taste than the bus driver. Clearly he picked your garage. Good luck finding his people.

comments.author: gil_fenner
comments.body: We had a stray in March and the owner came forward on the community page within a day. Post a photo of him there, that works best.

author: nadia_sorokina
subject: Lost rabbit, white lop named Pretzel
body: Our lop rabbit Pretzel got out of the back yard on Tibbets Court this afternoon, probably through a thin spot in the hedge by the fence. She is white with a gray patch over one eye, about the size of a small cat, and very friendly if you crouch down and let her come to you. Please check under porches and around the storm drain across the walk. I'm searching every block tonight with a carrier and a bag of carrots.

comments.author: ben_hollister
comments.body: Hi Nadia, I'm new, but I saw a white rabbit near the creek path off Quenby Road this morning. It may not be yours, but I thought you should know.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Carrots work, but don't chase her. Lay the carrier on its side with the open end in the grass by the storm drain and check it every hour. Lop rabbits freeze when they're scared, so they stay put.

comments.author: raj_pandey
comments.body: I'll walk the trail loop at dusk with a flashlight and look along the creek. Pretzel is adorable in the photo.

comments.author: nadia_sorokina
comments.body: Curtis, thanks, I'm doing exactly that. The carrier is out and the carrots are in it.

comments.author: greta_oseland
comments.body: Shared on the gardeners group and the ridge dog owners group. The gray patch over the eye is easy to spot, so people will know her.

comments.author: nadia_sorokina
comments.body: She's back! Found her under the neighbor's shed eating clover like nothing happened. Thank you all for the carrots, the carrier, and the shares.

comments.author: colleen_brandt
comments.body: Yay, so glad! Pretzel is a lucky girl. Thanks Curtis and Greta by name, you two are the best.

author: corinne_avila
subject: Missing indoor cat Clover, please check sheds
body: Our indoor cat Clover, a dark gray tabby with a white chin, has been missing since Tuesday afternoon, when the back door was left open for a delivery. She is shy and will hide under cars or sheds if she gets scared. She wears a blue collar with a tag and has a microchip, but we never registered it. We have flyers up on Oriel Street, Ashgrove Court, and the path by the bus stop, so please check sheds and crawl spaces.

comments.author: tess_harmon
comments.body: Oh no, Corinne. Sending calm thoughts. Shy cats often come out at night near food, so put a plate of wet food by the shed with an old towel nearby.

comments.author: samir_qureshi
comments.body: Sorry. I checked the crawl space under our deck last night and found nothing but a hornet nest. I'm happy to look again tomorrow morning.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: I'll post in the parents circle and the ridge dog owners group, that's where the cat people are. Clover is a lovely girl in that photo.

comments.author: fiona_rawlings
comments.body: Found a cat once in a shed here in Greaves Mill after nine days. Check behind the water heater and in any cubby hole, because they hide flat. Leave the door cracked a few inches at night.

comments.author: corinne_avila
comments.body: Thank you, Fiona. I'll check behind the water heater tonight.

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Community organizer hat on: I'll add Clover to the block alerts and tag the neighbors on Ashgrove Court by name. Corinne, message me your number so sightings come straight to you.

comments.author: corinne_avila
comments.body: Yes please, Imani, thank you so much. Her name is Clover.

author: odessa_wright
subject: Found small terrier mix on Gorse Lane
body: Found a small black-and-white terrier mix on Gorse Lane this morning. She has no collar or tags and is very friendly. She sat down when I said her name, so we have been calling her Pepper for now, but she may have a name of her own. I took her to the vet on Brindle Road and they scanned for a chip, with no luck. She is at our house in a crate with water, so please message me if she's yours.

comments.author: hal_brenneman
comments.body: Before you call the shelter, post her in the ridge dog owners group with the photo. Owners look there first, and the shelter's lost-dog list updates every day.

comments.author: sadie_kimbrough
comments.body: Oh, she's so sweet! I'm new to town, so which vet would you recommend for a nervous dog? Anyone know?

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: Terrier mixes that get out often slipped a fence line. Check the dog walk path on Gorse Lane for gaps, and call animal control on Monday if no one has claimed her.

comments.author: odessa_wright
comments.body: Thanks Deb, I'll walk the path after my shift and check the gaps.

comments.author: theo_marchetti
comments.body: Sorry, I'm new so I don't know the area. I'm glad she has a warm crate tonight.

comments.author: priya_lakhani
comments.body: That's our Juniper! She slipped out through the back gate Sunday night and we have been searching ever since. Thank you so much, we're on our way right now.

comments.author: odessa_wright
comments.body: So glad! Bring a leash and a treat, she's a sweetheart and has been very good company.

author: jonah_fitch
subject: Lost keys in the Halsey Crossing lot, orange carabiner
body: Lost a set of keys in the Halsey Crossing shopping lot on Thursday, somewhere between the grocery door and my car. There are three keys on a bright orange carabiner with a tiny plastic duck clipped to it. One key is for our front door, so I would really like it back. If you found them, drop them at the pizza place's counter or message me. Yes, I know the duck is ridiculous.

comments.author: gabriel_nunez
comments.body: Nothing turned in yet, but I'll keep a bin by the register for the next few days. The duck will be memorable.

comments.author: odessa_wright
comments.body: Check the customer service desk at the grocery store, and ask them to look near the cart corral. Keys often slide under a car parked next to the corral.

comments.author: remy_castellano
comments.body: I lost keys in that lot last spring and someone turned them in to the store within a day. Good luck, Jonah!

comments.author: jonah_fitch
comments.body: Odessa, I checked the desk and nothing. The cart corral idea is genius, I'll go back tomorrow.

comments.author: vivian_oduya
comments.body: Sorry about your keys. I lost mine twice this year. A tracker tag on the ring is a cheap fix, and it's how I found mine in a laundry bag.

author: gil_fenner
subject: Found a brown leather wallet by the ball fields
body: Found a brown leather wallet in the grass near the ball fields off Sadler Run on Saturday afternoon. It has a driver's license, an insurance card, a library card, and a few photos, but no cash. I turned the license in at the county clerk's counter, but I haven't heard anything since. If it's yours, tell me what's inside and I'll hand it back.

comments.author: bernadette_hughes
comments.body: Gil, the usual route is to drop it at the county clerk's counter or mail it back. Staff there can match a license to its owner quickly.

comments.author: eli_stroud
comments.body: Lost a wallet at the feilds last summer and a coach held it for me. Ask the coaches at the ball fields tomorrow, they know everyone.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Wow, a good Samaritan in Millrace. Shocking. Somebody notify the paper.

comments.author: gil_fenner
comments.body: Eli, thanks, I'll ask the coaches first thing. Owen, the paper can wait.

author: june_akers
subject: Red school backpack left at the Oriel Street stop
body: A red school backpack was left at the Oriel Street bus stop on Tuesday morning. It has a green name tag that says Pim in marker, a reading log, and a lunch container, and nothing expensive. Nobody has claimed it at the school office yet. If it's your child's, send me a message and I'll get it back to them. I'm keeping it on our porch for now.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: I posted this in the Tallgrass Parents Circle too, June. Lots of kids use that stop, so someone will recognize the tag. The bus driver may also know whose it is.

comments.author: vivian_oduya
comments.body: Sorry, I'm new and don't know the stop well. Is the school office open before the bus? I can stop by tomorrow to ask.

comments.author: owen_pruitt
comments.body: Please tell me it's not the kid who keeps losing his shoes on the bus. I'll ask my three before dinner.

comments.author: june_akers
comments.body: Owen, I bet it's a different kid, the reading log has a name on it. Let's hope it isn't the shoe kid.

comments.author: mateo_gallegos
comments.body: I'll stop by the school office after lunch and ask if they have a lost-and-found bin. Happy to bring it to you.

comments.author: june_akers
comments.body: Thank you, Mateo, that would be wonderful.

author: casimir_lowe
subject: Hawk nest on the pole behind Hensley Road
body: There's a red-tailed hawk nest on the top crossarm of the pole behind the fence line off Hensley Road. There are two chicks, maybe three, and the parent has been dropping rabbits and squirrels on the transformer all week. Keep your distance from the pole, obviously. The line crew knows about it and won't move the nest unless it becomes a hazard. Please leave it alone and keep dogs on a leash in that field.

comments.author: ruth_ellery
comments.body: Lovely news. Hawks keep the voles down in my beds, and the voles are the real pests of this town. Please tell the crew to be gentle with the nest.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: I saw one like this over the fairgrounds in the spring, when my mail route took me past it. Keep fireworks well away from the nest in July.

comments.author: lloyd_sutter
comments.body: Good for them, but hawks will also take outdoor cats. Put a bell on yours and keep it in at dawn and dusk.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: Good point, Lloyd. My own cat wears a bell, and I keep the cats off the pole side of the yard.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: My kids want to see the chicks. How close can we stand without bothering the parents? Asking for the parents group.

comments.author: casimir_lowe
comments.body: From the road at the bottom of Hensley, with binoculars. Not closer than the mailbox.

author: bridget_mccourt
subject: THE DEER ARE BACK on Lintel Way
body: Three deer, a mom and two fawns, have been eating everything in the hosta bed on Lintel Way at dawn, and yes, I have tried the spray. The spray works until it rains, which around here is about every other day. They also tore the top off my tomato plant. I am not angry at them, only at my tomatoes for being so delicious. What keeps deer off your plants?

comments.author: ivan_kuzmenko
comments.body: Plant what they dislike: lavender, catmint, and yarrow. Cage the tomatoes with netting at least four feet high. Fawns won't clear a fence that tall, and the mother usually won't either.

comments.author: tess_harmon
comments.body: Oh, the fawns! Please don't chase them. I'd happily sit out there at dawn with a coffee and watch.

comments.author: lena_hoffer
comments.body: Sorry, I'm new. Is it normal for deer to come into town like this? I'd be scared of them crossing the road.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Lena, welcome! Deer are normal around here. They do cross the road at dawn, so slow down on Lintel Way in the morning.

comments.author: augustin_perrault
comments.body: I have seen the same three. They have shown no interest in my roses, which I consider an insult to the roses.

comments.author: raj_pandey
comments.body: The deer by the trailhead do the same. A motion sprinkler saved my lettuce. Not pretty, but it works.

author: walt_gerrity
subject: Owl on the old mill fence
body: Sat out by the old mill fence last night, near the water tower, and heard a barred owl going who-cooks-for-you, which is what my father always called them. I haven't heard that since before the new road went in. Then I saw him, a big gray shape on the fence post, who looked at me like I owed him rent. I'm no bird man, but I know an owl when one sits still long enough to be insulted by me.

comments.author: anton_pelc
comments.body: Walt, I heard the same bird on my ride home last week, past the culvert at dusk. Owls out here are a good sign the creek is still clean.

comments.author: fiona_rawlings
comments.body: Walt, did it have ear tufts? Barred owls have round heads with no tufts, and great horned owls have the tufts. Tell us what you heard so we can be sure.

comments.author: walt_gerrity
comments.body: No tufts, round head, dark eyes, and it went who-cooks-for-you, so I'll stick with barred.

comments.author: kofi_mensah
comments.body: Walt, you're right about the owl. Come by the diner for coffee and tell the story again, and I'll bring the extra cream.

comments.author: renata_ocampo
comments.body: Summary for those who missed it: an owl on the mill fence, probably a barred owl per Fiona, and Walt is delighted. Please keep cats indoors at dusk, since owls hunt them too.

comments.author: harlan_dietz
comments.body: Harlan here, I measured the fence post. It stands about two feet high, and the owl was well out of Walt's reach.

author: ansel_grieco
subject: The white van on Duncombe Lane is watching our porches
body: The same white cargo van with no lettering has parked on Duncombe Lane every weekday from about ten to noon, across from three houses that get packages. The driver walks up each walk, looks at the doorbell, and walks back. Two packages went missing from that stretch last week. I'm not saying it's a ring, but I think it's him, and somebody needs to ask the man in that van what he is doing. Keep packages inside if you can, and photograph the plate if the van shows up again.

comments.author: wendell_pike
comments.body: Ansel, two packages on a route is not evidence. Pull the dispatch log and ask the delivery companies for their route lists before you say him. A name in a post can follow someone for years.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: Ansel, the only white van I trust is the one bringing my ice cream on Sundays. Maybe the man is lost, or maybe he just likes doorbells.

comments.author: gunnar_sorensen
comments.body: That's probably a crew working on a roof up the block. They park on Duncombe every week while the job runs. Don't jump to him, ask the crew first.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: Every week for a month, Gunnar. That is not a roof job, that is a man with time on his hands and a doorbell fixation. I'm asking the question out loud.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: Please don't post a photo of the driver. Reporting the van to the non-emergency line is the right step. Give them the time, the plate, and the block, then leave the rest to them.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Parking on the public street is legal. You can't stop the man for parking.

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: I agree with Ruben on this. File the report and don't post a face. A van like that brought my sister's medicine last month, so it may be a pharmacy or a supply run.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Ansel, I'm with you. Stop being polite about it. Two packages in one week is a pattern, and somebody has to say so.

comments.author: tomasz_wojcik
comments.body: Ansel, you have a van problem and a mouth problem. Go mow your lawn and quit making things up about people.
